items.title: King consents to emergency declaration in Serian
items.summary: KUALA LUMOUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has consented to the declaration of an emergency throughout the Serian, Sarawak following worsening haze. In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision was made after taking into consideration the advice of the Prime Minister and the Sarawak Premier, as well as relevant agencies, regarding air quality levels in the affected area. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Anwar tells Rural Development Ministry and MOF to find middle ground in funding row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today called on the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to resolve issues concerning allocations, including delayed payments to contractors, through discussions. On Thursday, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said there were no restrictions on KKDW allocations for rural road projects, with the full allocation for the projects having already been channelled. The issue arose following a statement by Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi regarding problems faced by contractors following delays in payments for projects under his ministry.

items.title: Teen drowns off Pantai Klebang, mother mourns family's hope
items.summary: Mazan, a general assistant at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Bukit Rambai, said Arif, the youngest of two siblings, had been the family's hope of caring for his older sister, who has Down syndrome. She said the siblings shared a close bond, with Arif helping to attend to his sister's needs since he was young. "She kept saying, 'Arif, Arif'.

items.title: Court dismisses challenges to 2021 Parliament suspension during Covid-19 emergency
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today dismissed legal challenges by two lawmakers, the Malaysian Bar, Bersih 2.0 and several others over the suspension of Parliament during the 2021 Covid-19 emergency. Judge Datuk Aliza Sulaiman ruled that the court could not grant the declarations sought to invalidate provisions of the Emergency (Essential Powers) Ordinance 2021, including Section 14, which dealt with the suspension of Parliament. She dismissed the two judicial review applications and two originating summons with no order as to costs.

items.title: Anwar endorses proposal for SC or BNM oversight of Tabung Haji investments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today backed a proposal by Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to place its investment operations under the regulatory oversight of the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) or Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM). He said the initiative by TH’s new management, led by its chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain, was a positive step towards strengthening governance and accountability at the pilgrimage fund management institution. Yesterday, Abdul Rashid said TH was refining a new regulatory framework to place its investment operations under the statutory oversight of the SC.

items.title: WhatsApp engineers guide Nepal tunnel rescue as two workers found alive
items.summary: KATHMANDU: An army of experts in a WhatsApp group is guiding rescue workers scouring a Nepali valley after a huge flash flood more than a week ago as they desperately search for anyone who may be alive inside tunnels of devastated hydropower plants. One of them said there could be more survivors in the tunnels. Nepal's Independent Power Producers' Association said on Monday at least eight people could be trapped at Chilime, while an official at the Nepal Electricity Authority said 46 may be trapped at Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant, further south.

items.title: Nepal floods could cost insurers over US$130 million
items.summary: MUMBAI: The devastating flood in Nepal last week could result in commercial insurance losses exceeding 20 billion Nepali rupees (US$132.3 million), with hydropower projects accounting for most claims, according to a top official at one of the country's leading insurers. Eleven Nepali hydropower projects lie in the affected region, some covered by standard commercial insurance policies that are still being assessed, Toton Chakraborty, CEO of Oriental Insurance Company Nepal, told Reuters. Oriental Insurance Nepal, a unit of the New Delhi-based Indian insurer, is among the leading insurers in the region.

items.title: Hadi Awang expected to attend 2026 Umno General Assembly
items.summary: Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, who led the Umno delegation to the 72nd Pas Annual Muktamar in Pengkalan Chepa, Kelantan, today said Hadi has confirmed the matter to him. Asyraf said deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man during the muktamar also expressed his commitment to advancing Muslim unity. Earlier, Asyraf attended the 72nd Pas Muktamar at the Kelantan Islamic Education Centre (PUTIK), Pengkalan Chepa, Kelantan, representing Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

items.title: US Navy captain inspired by Sabah community's warmth
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: For US Navy Captain Robert Reyes, it has been a joy to be around the enthusiastic community here. He said he hoped improvements made at the school under the PP26 community project, including a gazebo and observation deck, would inspire students to realise their potential. Reyes said the school project, set against Sabah's scenic surroundings, was intended to provide students with an opportunity to broaden their minds and aspire to greater things.

items.title: Eight men charged with murder over fatal Taman Alam Megah brawl
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 4 — Eight men, including two alleged secret society members, were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of a man during a brawl involving a group of individuals in Taman Alam Megah last month. Puwaneswaran, 39; A. Rhubban, 37; K. Thivagar, 29; Shaik Hasanudin Ahlauwudin, 26; Sheikh Mauludin Ahlauwudin, 24; and R. Darvin Raj, 23, nodded after the charge was read out to them before Magistrate Cynthia Noor Haizean Sulaiman. The remaining accused were unrepresented.

items.title: Anwar: MoF, KKDW should resolve rural road project payment issues amicably
items.summary: In 2022, the ministry spent its entire RM1.1 billion allocation. However, expenditure rose significantly in subsequent years, reaching RM1.8 billion against a RM1.1 billion budget in 2023, RM2 billion against a RM1.3 billion budget in 2024, and RM2.3 billion against a RM1.6 billion budget in 2025. For 2026, KKDW had already spent RM1.9 billion of its approved RM2.1 billion allocation as of June.

items.title: Prosecution to appeal Rosmah ruling allowing additional evidence, says AG
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 4 — The prosecution will appeal the Court of Appeal’s decision allowing Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence for corruption involving the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project. “It merits an appeal to the Federal Court. On Tuesday, a three-man bench of the Court of Appeal comprising Justices Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and K. Muniandy allowed Rosmah’s application to submit additional evidence in her appeal against her corruption conviction and sentence.

items.title: MAG to continue fuel hedging in 2027 as jet fuel costs rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) will continue hedging its fuel costs in 2027 as soaring jet fuel prices put pressure on its finances and prompt the group to trim parts of its network. MAG president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said the sharp increase in jet fuel prices had put significant pressure on the group's financial performance, prompting a targeted five per cent cut to its network. Fuel accounts for about 40 per cent of MAG's total costs, with every US$1 increase in jet fuel prices translating into an estimated RM50 million increase in annual costs.

items.title: Court rules DNAA not applicable in Maju Holdings director, wife’s CBT, money laundering case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — The Sessions Court here has rejected an application for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) in the criminal breach of trust (CBT) and money laundering case involving Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd director Tan Sri Abu Sahid Mohamed and his wife. Abu Sahid claimed trial to 17 charges involving CBT and money laundering linked to the proposed MEX II Highway project on September 8 last year. He faces four CBT charges involving RM313 million and 13 money laundering charges involving RM139 million, allegedly committed between May 2016 and October 2019.

items.title: [UPDATED] 35 cloud-seeding operations this year, 90pct yield rain
items.summary: The Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES) said the operations targeted selected areas and water catchments in Perlis, Kedah, Perak, Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Sarawak and Sabah. It said the operations were carried out as an early intervention against dry weather, low rainfall and the risk of deteriorating air quality. NRES said cloud seeding remained dependent on atmospheric conditions and suitable cloud formation.

items.title: Court of Appeal upholds death sentence for deaf, mute man over brutal murder
items.summary: However, the circumstances did not prevent a three-member Court of Appeal panel today from upholding the death sentence against Kang Chang Heng, 47, after unanimously dismissing the former furniture factory worker's appeal to set aside his conviction and sentence. "Therefore, we uphold the death sentence imposed on the appellant (Kang)," she said. Noorin said the court had also considered Kang's defence that he had borrowed money from an illegal moneylender by providing the victims' home address as collateral.

items.title: BN backs unity govt despite push for earlier GE16, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Barisan Nasional remains committed to the unity government and the country’s political stability despite calls within the coalition for the 16th General Election (GE16) to be held earlier, said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir. The Star reported that Zambry said BN’s support for the unity government remained firm, stressing that calls for an earlier election should not be interpreted as confidence that the coalition would automatically regain federal power. He said there was no intention among BN’s partners to undermine or bring down the unity government before the next general election.

items.title: No more MACC orange uniform for political leaders in court — Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Political leaders will be given leeway not to wear the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) orange uniform when brought to court, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. "Yesterday, I also conveyed that before prosecution, when they are brought before the court and charged, they do not need to wear the orange (MACC) uniform. "If you want to investigate, investigate first.

items.title: Anwar backs tighter oversight of Tabung Haji investments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has backed tighter regulatory oversight of Lembaga Tabung Haji's (TH) investments, including possible supervision by the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) or Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM). Anwar said the measure was necessary to prevent abuse of power and other irregularities in TH's management. "This is a measure being taken by the new TH management, led by Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain.

items.title: Malaysian man jailed six years in Australia for keeping Indonesian woman as slave
items.summary: MELBOURNE, Sept 4 — A Malaysian man has been sentenced to six years in prison in Australia after being convicted of enslaving and assaulting an Indonesian woman. Free Malaysia Today, citing ABC News, reported that Melbourne County Court Judge Michael Cahill sentenced Chong Chee Kit, 47, after a jury found him guilty of forcing the woman into domestic servitude and subjecting her to repeated abuse. A jury in May found Chong guilty of keeping the woman, who was in her 60s, in slavery between February and October 2022.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines returns to Busan after 28 years, Firefly enters China
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines Bhd will resume flights to Busan on Dec 2 after a 28-year absence, while sister airline FlyFirefly Sdn Bhd (Firefly) will make its first foray into China with direct services to Kunming. Malaysia Airlines will operate four weekly Kuala Lumpur-Busan flights using Boeing B737-8 aircraft, marking its return to South Korea's second-largest city after last serving the route between 1996 and 1998. Upon resumption, Malaysia Airlines will be the only carrier offering non-stop flights between Kuala Lumpur and Busan.

items.title: Penang steps up action to curb sewage pollution from pig farms in Kampung Selamat
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 4 — The Penang state government has taken several measures to address sewage pollution from pig farms in Kampung Selamat, near Tasek Gelugor, including requiring all farms in the area to send their wastewater to a biogas plant in Ampang Jajar. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman Jason H’ng Mooi Lye said the move is part of the state government’s efforts to prevent livestock farm sewage from being discharged directly into drains or rivers in the area. “The matter was discussed at a meeting with the state Veterinary Services Department and the state assemblyman for the area in April, and the state government has required all pig farms in Kampung Selamat to send their sewage waste to the biogas plant in Ampang Jajar since May.

items.title: Anwar to discuss further action on Sarawak haze with Abang Jo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Further action, including the possibility of declaring a disaster emergency following an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeding 500 in Serian, will be discussed with the Sarawak government, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said he had contacted Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg yesterday to discuss the matter. This morning, air quality in Serian, Sarawak, remained at a hazardous level, with the monitoring station at the local District Police Headquarters (IPD) recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 518.

items.title: NCID strengthens global drug enforcement ties at Argentina conference
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman's Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) is looking to forge closer cooperation with international enforcement agencies, including the United States Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), as Malaysia steps up efforts against transnational drug trafficking. NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the department was also looking forward to strengthening cooperation with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) on Drugs, particularly in intelligence sharing and efforts to counter emerging narcotics threats. Hussein, who led the Malaysian delegation, said the four-day conference provided enforcement agencies with an important platform to exchange experiences and strengthen international networks.

items.title: Guan Eng calls for action against Zahid over KKDW overspending
items.summary: Lim said Finance Ministry (MoF) figures showed KKDW spending exceeded its approved allocation in each of the past three years. In 2023, KKDW spent RM1.8 billion against an allocation of RM1.1 billion, while spending in 2024 reached RM2 billion compared with RM1.3 billion allocated. In 2025, the ministry spent RM2.3 billion against an approved allocation of RM1.6 billion.

items.title: Kerjaya Prospek's maiden data centre job seen yielding 5-7pct margin
items.summary: The firm said the latest contract accounts for about 15 per cent of KPG's RM5.9 billion outstanding order book. Kenanga Research raised its FY26 and FY27 job win assumptions to RM3.5 billion and RM2.5 billion, respectively, from RM2.5 billion and RM2.2 billion previously. It also raised its revenue recognition assumptions to RM2.6 billion and RM3.0 billion from RM2.35 billion and RM2.65 billion, respectively.

items.title: A-GC to appeal ruling allowing Rosmah to adduce fresh evidence
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Attorney-General's Chambers will appeal against the Court of Appeal's decision allowing Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor to adduce additional evidence in the RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid project corruption case. On Sept 1, a three-member Court of Appeal bench allowed Rosmah's application to introduce fresh evidence involving prosecution witness Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, who testified as the 16th prosecution witness during the trial. The bench, chaired by Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, ruled that Rosmah had established a prima facie case for the admission of the additional evidence.

items.title: Harmonised standards, 'single window' clearance key to seamless JS-SEZ cross-border trade
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Establishing a single-window trade system and harmonising regulatory standards between Malaysia and Singapore are vital steps to achieve seamless cross-border integration and fully unlock the economic potential of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), according to a leading express logistics company. FedEx Malaysia managing director Woon Tien Long highlighted that despite strong bilateral trade ties, compliance with distinct national regulatory frameworks requires streamlined coordination. "A single window of trade would be able to unlock this seamlessness, eliminating the need to apply for double import permits," he told a recent interview session during the FedEx Johor-Singapore Cross-Border Media Tour at FedEx South Pacific Regional Hub Singapore.

items.title: Azalina calls for red flags at Desaru beaches after three teens drown
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — Pengerang Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has called for coastal areas in Desaru, including Pantai Tanjung Lompat, to be equipped with red flags and warning signs to deter people from swimming in high-risk areas. She said she had proposed the measure to the local authorities (PBT), particularly for beaches with strong currents that are unsuitable for swimming. She said visitors might not be aware of the risks, particularly at campsites without clear signs prohibiting swimming.

items.title: Almost 99pc Malaysia Airlines cabin crew drug tested, all negative
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: About 98.8 per cent of Malaysia Airlines cabin crew have undergone drug screening, with all tests returning negative, said Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG). MAG managing director and chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said drug screening would be made a mandatory annual requirement for all cabin crew. Nasaruddin said MAG had also completed drug screening for more than 1,500 pilots across its airlines, including all pilots and cabin crew of Firefly, on Aug 15.

items.title: Lorry driver remanded three days over crash that killed 12-year-old boy in Gurun
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Police have detained a 40-year-old lorry driver over a crash involving a motorcycle on Jalan Gurun-Jeniang yesterday that killed a 12-year-old boy. The victim, Muhammad Ilham Firdaus Mohamad Iruan, 12, died at the scene from severe injuries. Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the suspect was detained to assist investigations into the crash, Harian Metro reported.

items.title: Economy Ministry examines Malaysia's preparedness for an ageing nation in 2027 Budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Economy Ministry is examining the structure of the country's preparedness as Malaysia moves towards becoming an ageing nation, through Budget 2027. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said this is important to ensure the sustainability and continuity of the country's economic growth, as well as to empower the next generation. "The younger generation needs to shoulder greater responsibility for the sustainability of the economy and the continuity of the country's growth (as we transition to an ageing nation).

items.title: Two trapped tunnel workers rescued in Nepal 'miracle'
items.summary: KATHMANDU, (Nepal): Two hydropower workers were pulled alive from a tunnel buried by debris in Nepal on Friday, a rare ray of hope on the tenth day of rescue efforts after catastrophic Himalayan flooding. Rescuers cheered as one man was pulled through a muddy opening, a video released by the energy ministry showed. Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said in a statement.

items.title: Retired military officer with ‘Datuk’ title charged over alleged caddie molestation in Ayer Keroh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — A 68-year-old retired military officer holding the title “Datuk” was charged in the Ayer Keroh Magistrates’ Court here today with using criminal force with intent to outrage the modesty of a 20-year-old female caddie last month. The charge alleged that Yahya used criminal force against the victim with intent to outrage her modesty at the Tiara Melaka Golf & Country Club golf course in Jalan Gapam, Bukit Katil, in Ayer Keroh, Melaka, between 8.30am and 12.30pm on August 25. The court was also told that Yahya had a prostate-related health condition requiring treatment.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar open to consider early general election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is open to considering calls for an early general election. Anwar, however, said any decision would be made after careful consideration before being presented to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong. However, Anwar said the government's immediate focus remained on the economy, the welfare of the people and efforts to rid the country of corruption and abuse of power.

items.title: Citi eyes China brokerage unit licence as soon as this month
items.summary: HONG KONG: Citigroup expects to get regulatory approval for its wholly-owned China brokerage business as soon as this month and plans to add several dozen staff at the unit over the next few months, said two people with knowledge of the matter. Citi declined to comment. The China expansion would see Citi competing with already licensed Wall Street rivals including JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley for a share of growing and increasingly profitable onshore securities trading and underwriting deals.

items.title: PN yet to decide Bersatu's position in coalition, says Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) has yet to decide on Bersatu's position in the coalition following Pas' decision to end its political cooperation with the party. PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the matter would be discussed at a special meeting, although no date had been set. Tuan Ibrahim said so far Bersatu remained a member of PN.

items.title: Singapore's tax revenue up 9.4pct to S$97.3bil
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore collected S$97.3 billion (S$1=RM3.19) in tax revenue for financial year (FY) 2025/2026, up by 9.4 per cent compared with the preceding year amid stronger economic activity and consumer spending, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) said. In a statement today, IRAS said the total tax revenue collected accounts for 74.8 per cent of the Singapore Government's operating revenue and 12.3 per cent of Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP). "The arrears rate for income tax, Goods and Services Tax (GST), and property tax remains low at 0.64 per cent of net tax assessed," the statement said.

items.title: Lorry driver arrested over crash that killed 12-year-old motorcyclist
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: Police have arrested a lorry driver involved in an accident that killed a 12-year-old boy who was riding a motorcycle along Jalan Gurun-Jeniang yesterday. The victim, Muhammad Ilham Firdaus Mohamad Iruan, died at the scene from severe injuries. Kuala Muda police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the 40-year-old man was detained to assist with investigations.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Putrajaya, Sarawak in talks over Serian haze as API breaches 500
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The federal government is in discussions with the Sarawak government over the worsening haze in Serian, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) has breached 500. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had been in contact with Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg, with both sides discussing further measures to address the situation. Anwar said the government would also consider cloud seeding and other measures to alleviate the haze.

items.title: Perlis police arrest activist over incendiary TikTok on Sri Veera Maha Kaliamman Kovil temple
items.summary: KANGAR, Sept 4 — A 55-year-old activist has been remanded for two days from today on suspicion of making an inciting post via social media related to the organisation of a gathering concerning the demolition of a Hindu temple here on Aug 22. Kangar district police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the man, who works as a consultant, was arrested in Petaling Jaya, Selangor yesterday at 10 am. He said that earlier, the Perlis police received 14 reports regarding posts on the activist’s TikTok application between Aug 22 and 27.

items.title: Serian API hits 521 as Sarawak haze reaches hazardous levels
items.summary: Two locations recorded very unhealthy readings — Samarahan (284) and Sri Aman (235). Meanwhile, 11 locations recorded unhealthy readings: Sarikei (182), Sibu (181), Mukah (177), Bintulu (157), Kota Kinabalu (152), Tawau (151), Samalaju (146), Sandakan (140), Pasir Gudang, Johor (128), Segamat, Johor (115), and Miri (112). API readings are updated hourly based on data from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: 'Sayang, you ok?': Malaysian's last words to wife before fatal stabbing in South Korea
items.summary: RAWANG: The widow of a Malaysian who was stabbed to death while trying to break up a fight in South Korea in July said her husband managed to check on her in his dying moments. Nurcahaya Ruslan, 34, said her husband, Ahmad Shah Ahmad Ros, 26, was bleeding heavily from his stab wound, but still made his way to her. She said her husband then received a call from a friend who needed help.

items.title: Third missing teenager’s body recovered at Kota Tinggi beach
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — The body of a third missing teenager has been recovered from the waters near Tanjung Siang, following a tragic incident at Tanjung Lompat in Bandar Penawar. The victim, 16-year-old Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal, was found floating by the search and rescue (SAR) team and members of the public at 11.15am today, approximately five kilometres from the site of the initial incident. Kota Tinggi deputy police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad confirmed the discovery.

items.title: MAG says mass drug screenings for Malaysia Airlines crew near 100pc
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has completed drug screenings for nearly all Malaysia Airlines cabin crew following the arrest of a pilot in Jakarta, president and group chief executive officer Capt. Nasaruddin A. Bakar said today. On Aug 17, MAG announced that all operationally active Malaysia Airlines pilots had undergone drug tests and tested negative.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines resumes Busan flights starting December
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Malaysia Airlines will resume flights to Busan, South Korea's second-largest city, starting December this year as the national carrier expands its network and pushes to return to profitability. Malaysian Aviation Group chief executive officer Capt Nasaruddin A. Bakar said the Busan service is one of several new routes the airline group expects to launch, including expansion by its budget unit Firefly, which recently added China's Kunming to its destination network. MORE TO COME

items.title: Two dead in Jasin motorcycle crash after overtaking manoeuvre fails
items.summary: Jasin district police chief Supt Lee Robert said both victims, a 21-year-old college student and a 41-year-old lorry driver, died on the spot in the incident, which occurred at about 11.30 pm. He said initial investigations found that the student was travelling from Bemban towards Ayer Keroh, while the lorry driver was heading in the opposite direction, towards Bemban from Ayer Keroh. Lee said police were unable to obtain any CCTV or dashcam footage of the incident.

items.title: Tahfiz students perform prayers to support search for missing teens in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — For the second consecutive day, students of Madrasah Tahfiz Al-Quran Ar-Redha in Bandar Penawar recited the azan and Yasin and performed Dhuha and hajat prayers as the search continued for two teenagers feared drowned at Tanjung Lompat Beach here. Islamic Education teacher Mohd Azroy Azhar said the students took the initiative voluntarily after seeing the various efforts by the authorities and the victims’ families to locate the missing teenagers. He said the students were also doing their part by offering prayers and supplications, hoping that the two missing teenagers would be found soon.

items.title: PAS sets seven priorities for GE16, including wider political cooperation
items.summary: The New Straits Times reported that PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the party’s Muslim unity agenda would see it continue defending Islam while honouring agreements reached with other parties. “PAS is prepared to cooperate with any party on matters that benefit the country without compromising its policies and principles,” he said. Abdul Hadi was speaking when delivering his policy speech at the opening of PAS’ 72nd Annual Muktamar in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, today.

items.title: Police refer case of man accused of provoking crowd at National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya to DPP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Police are awaiting further instructions from the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) after referring an investigation paper on a man accused of causing a disturbance and provoking the crowd during the National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on August 31. Putrajaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed said the investigation paper was referred to the DPP’s office yesterday for further action, BuletinTV3 reported. Police had previously reported that a man was detained for allegedly causing a disturbance and provoking members of the public during the National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on Monday.

items.title: Serian API hits hazardous 518, emergency declaration possible
items.summary: SERIAN, Sept 4 — Serian recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 518 as of 10 am today, placing it in the “hazardous” category amid transboundary haze. According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), an API reading above 300 is classified as hazardous, while readings between 201 and 300 are categorised as “very unhealthy”. Kuching also recorded a hazardous API reading of 310, followed by Kota Samarahan at 281 and Sri Aman at 245.

items.title: Six held over Malaysian co-pilot’s Jakarta drug case after four fled to Thailand, Vietnam and returned
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Bukit Aman’s Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (JSJN) has detained six local men over a drug smuggling case involving a Malaysian co-pilot arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang, Banten, Indonesia, with four of the suspects having fled to Thailand and Vietnam after learning of his arrest. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the six were believed to have acted as suppliers and couriers who provided drugs to the co-pilot. Meanwhile, Harian Metro reported that Hussein said two of the suspects had fled to Thailand while another two went to Vietnam after learning of the co-pilot’s arrest.

items.title: Appeals court grants Najib and son stay of bankruptcy action in RM1.7b tax case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 4 — The Court of Appeal here today granted former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak and his son, Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin, a stay of bankruptcy proceedings against them. A three-man bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Ong Chee Kwan allowed their appeals to set aside the High Court’s decision on Nov 17 last year, which had dismissed their applications for a stay. Najib and Nazifuddin had sought a stay of the bankruptcy proceedings pending the disposal of their appeals before the SCIT against additional tax assessments issued by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).

items.title: EC reaffirms commitment to fairness and transparency on 69th anniversary
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — The Election Commission (EC), which marks its 69th anniversary today, has reaffirmed its commitment to managing the country’s electoral process fairly, transparently, efficiently and with integrity. “May the EC continue to move forward with integrity and remain a trusted democratic institution in safeguarding and strengthening the country’s democratic process. “The EC, efficient and transparent,” according to the post.

items.title: Three girls caught fighting in viral social media video in Kuala Pilah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Police are investigating a fight involving three teenage girls that went viral on social media after the incident at Dataran Melang in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan. Online, Kuala Pilah district police chief Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin said the incident involved a 15-year-old schoolgirl who went to the location with her brother to meet two acquaintances over a misunderstanding linked to the circulation of her photograph on social media. Muhamad Mustafah said the girl and her father later went to the home of one of the individuals yesterday to discuss the matter before lodging a police report.

items.title: PAS does not need manifesto pledge on gambling ban, says Kedah MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — PAS does not need to include its opposition to gambling in its election manifesto because the stance is already part of the party’s core principles, said Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor. Sanusi, who is also PAS central election director, said the public could refer to Clause 5 of the PAS Constitution, which clearly states that the party seeks to uphold Islamic values and laws in governance, including Syariah laws prohibiting gambling premises and regulating the sale of alcohol, Berita Harian reported. Read the PAS Constitution.

items.title: Man injured in suspected shooting at Machang Bubok used car workshop
items.summary: Seberang Perai Tengah district police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said police received a report on the incident at about 2.05pm. “One of the suspects is believed to have fired a shot towards the victim,” he said in a statement today. Nik Aminuddin said police are investigating to identify the suspects and establish the motive.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng calls for action against Zahid over RM2.1b Rural Development Ministry overspending
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — DAP’s Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has called for Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and the Rural and Regional Development Ministry to face action after the ministry spent RM2.1 billion more than its approved allocations over three years. Lim said allowing spending beyond approved allocations could set a bad precedent, with other ministries potentially repeating the practice in ways that could affect the national treasury and financial stability. Lim cited Finance Ministry figures showing the ministry spent RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an approved allocation of RM1.1 billion.

items.title: Johari Abdul: Parliament must tackle Malaysia’s ageing, smaller families through effective legislation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Parliament must translate demographic challenges such as ageing populations, smaller families and changing intergenerational needs into concrete laws, budgets and policies, said Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul. He said population and development issues were ultimately political questions as public priorities must find expression through legislation, institutions and government spending. Pressure creates priorities and priorities eventually appear in legislation, institutions and budgets,” he said at a welcome dinner he hosted for participants of the Asian Forum of Parliamentarians on Population and Development (AFPPD) Annual Conference 2026 here yesterday.

items.title: ‘Snow’ on Kesas? It was actually soap foam after heavy rain
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — What looked like snow covering part of the Shah Alam Expressway (Kesas) yesterday afternoon turned out to be soap foam triggered by heavy rain washing up residue from a spill more than a week ago. Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said initial investigations found the soap residue likely came from a lorry load that spilled on August 24 near the Kota Kemuning slip road before the vehicle entered Kesas heading towards Klang, Kosmo! “However, heavy rain today caused the remaining soap residue to produce foam along about 500 metres of the highway,” he added.
